doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Reading and the daily trip to Charleston High School
summary: He does not recall reading much; he rode the bus or bicycle 14 miles on gravel to Charleston High School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So as a kid, you’re picking up all of these musical cues, it sounds like, just in a very natural way. Were you a reader? I guess if your mother was a schoolteacher...
I didn’t learn to read...
Not music. He’s talking about reading.
Oh, yeah. Well, I don’t know when I started reading.
Well, you read a lot always when I knew you. I remember that you were always recommending books to me when we wrote.
I’d imagine that if your mom was a schoolteacher, the ABCs were right there in front of you.
Yes.
Did you stay in Tippo all the way through high school, or did you move to a town?

No. I took the bus from Tippo to Charleston, 14 miles. Charleston High School was in the hills. The Delta went to the hills 14 miles... That was the beginning of the hills, at Charleston High School. I don’t know... I used to ride the bicycle to... I think that Charleston...I don’t...
On a gravel road?
Yes.
You would sometimes ride a bicycle to school.
Yeah.
14 miles. I didn’t know that.
Yeah, well...I don’t know...
It was a rough road. I remember going with your mother 60 miles an hour on that road!
60 miles an hour on the gravel road.
Oh, yeah, absolutely. Anybody on that road down there... Until it got really big ruts. Then they’d come and put more gravel down.
A place where you could really use a four-wheel drive.
I think they had Oldsmobiles or something, and they were worn out at 50,000 miles for sure.
